title: Start at Main
plain: Main is the method where this program starts. Its first instruction asks CreateSampleProjects to run. Main waits at this line until that method returns a list.
say: The application starts in Main. This line calls a method that creates our three fictional projects and gives them back as a list.
why: A separate sample-data method keeps the long example values out of the menu code.
next: Follow the call to CreateSampleProjects.
terms: List<Project>
The type: a list holding Project object references. List is a class supplied by .NET. <Project> specifies what goes in it.
projects
A local variable name that will refer to the returned list. It is not a class or a method.
CreateSampleProjects()
A method call. Parentheses call it; empty parentheses mean we pass no input values.
= assigns the returned value to projects. The semicolon ends this instruction.
public static async Task Main()
public allows access. static means no Program object is needed. async permits awaiting work. Task represents work that can complete later; it is not our fictional project task.

title: Create the project objects
plain: CreateSampleProjects makes Website, Inventory, and Training, in that order. Here we focus on the second object, Inventory. new Project(...) calls the constructor below, then the { ... } initializer fills in the task, milestone, and risk information.
say: I used one Project class to describe the data. new creates an individual object. Inventory is one object, and its properties hold its own values.
why: One fixed task, milestone, and risk avoids a second layer of item objects. A second risk would require extending the design.

blocks.label: One of the three example objects
The constructor called by new Project(...)

next: CreateSampleProjects finishes Training, then returns the list to Main.

Project is the type; inventory is a variable referring to this new object.
new Project(2, ... )
Creates a Project and runs its constructor. The arguments become id, name, and manager.
Id = id
Copies the input parameter id into this object's property Id. Capitalization distinguishes the names.
{ TaskTitle = ... }
An object initializer: sets properties after the constructor finishes. Commas separate assignments.
ChangeStatus(3, ItemStatus.Open)
Makes this project's risk Open. Section 3 means risk. New projects initially have a Closed risk and NotStarted work.
more: The website's task and milestone start Completed. Training's milestone is overdue and InProgress, but its risk is Closed. Initial values are invented classroom data, not generated by AI.

title: Return to Main with the list
plain: The method returns one list containing references to the three existing Project objects. Main stores a reference to that list in projects. It then creates the object it will use for HTTP requests and prints the title.
say: This is how the methods connect: the sample-data method returns a list, and Main continues with that list. Nothing is saved to a database.
why: The same objects stay in memory during this run. Other methods can change them, and later calculations see those changes.
values: One HttpClient object for local requests
next: The program reaches the menu loop.
terms: return
Ends this method and supplies a value to its caller. Here it returns to Main, not out of the application.
new List<Project> { ... }
Creates a list of references to the three existing objects. It does not copy all their data.
using HttpClient client = new HttpClient()
Creates a .NET request-sending object. using releases it when Main ends. This line does not call Qwen.
Timeout
Limits an HTTP request to 120 seconds. The separate model-list request has a shorter limit.

title: The menu chooses a method
plain: The loop displays five choices and waits for a typed line. For this walkthrough, enter 3. switch chooses the matching case and calls UpdateStatus with the project list.
say: while keeps the menu available. switch routes the user's choice to a method. Here option three calls UpdateStatus.
why: A small menu needs a clear set of choices, not a framework or graphical interface.

blocks.label: Read the menu choice and call its method

next: UpdateStatus will select a project.

WriteLine prints text; ReadLine waits for a line of input.
string? choice
The input is text. ? also allows null if input ends.
choice?.Trim()
Remove outer spaces if choice is not null. ?. avoids calling a method on a missing value.
case "3"
The branch matching typed text 3. It passes projects to UpdateStatus.
break
Leaves the switch when the called method finishes; the while loop then shows the menu again.
more: Option 1 calls ShowProjects. Option 2 calls ViewProject. Option 4 follows the separate Local AI route in this guide. Option 5 exits. The program does not execute all methods just because they appear lower in the file.

title: Select Inventory System
plain: UpdateStatus calls SelectProject. That method first calls ShowProjects, which prints each project's current health. Then you enter project ID 2. The search returns the existing Inventory object, and UpdateStatus continues.
say: The selection method turns the user's typed ID into the Project object the rest of this operation will use.
why: Returning the existing object means changes affect the same project already in the list. We do not need to copy changes back.

blocks.label: Find and return the chosen project

next: Back in UpdateStatus, choose which part of the project to change.
terms: private static void UpdateStatus(List<Project> projects)
A method inside Program. private limits it to that class. static needs no Program instance. void returns no result value, but the method can still change objects. projects is its input list.
Project?
This method may return a Project reference or null, meaning no valid selection.
TryParse(input, out int id)
Checks whether input is a whole number. On success the converted number is placed in id.

Visits each Project object in the list.

if (selectedProject == null) return
Stop this menu action when selection failed or was cancelled. Main will show the menu again.
more: The full call chain is Main → UpdateStatus → SelectProject → ShowProjects → each project's CalculateHealth. Each calculation returns to ShowProjects; it returns to SelectProject, which returns the chosen object to UpdateStatus. The guide keeps that chain visible here instead of asking you to navigate the files.

title: Choose the risk section
plain: Enter 3 to choose the risk. This section number selects a group of properties on Project. There is no item ID 203 anymore.
say: This first block selects the project and the part to change. It checks the number before moving on.
why: Fixed choices fit the smaller design: one task, one milestone, and one risk per project.

title: Show choices, then read Closed
plain: The Project method returns [Open, Closed] for section 3. UpdateStatus prints those choices as 1 and 2. Enter 2. The code checks the input is a valid menu number.
say: This second block gets valid choices from the Project class and validates what the user typed.
why: The menu and the change method reuse the same allowed-status rule. A risk cannot be changed to Completed.
next: Convert menu number 2 into list position 1, then apply Closed.

A list of enum values. ItemStatus is a type with named choices, not a class or method.
GetAllowedStatuses(section)
A method call with the input 3. Its return becomes allowedStatuses.

Start an index at zero, repeat while it is inside the list, and add one after each pass.
i + 1 / allowedStatuses[i]
Show people a number starting at 1, while reading the list at positions starting at 0.
statusNumber > allowedStatuses.Count
Reject numbers beyond the displayed choices before using them as a list position.

title: Change the existing Project object
plain: Menu number 2 becomes list position 1, which contains Closed. ChangeStatus checks that value again, assigns RiskStatus, and returns true.
say: This third block makes the actual change. The selected Project object is the same object stored in our list, so its RiskStatus now holds Closed.
why: The status properties have private setters. Other code uses ChangeStatus, so invalid requests are rejected before assignment.

blocks.label: Block 3: choose the value and call the change
Reference declaration · the protected status property

values: The Closed value passed by the caller
next: Return true to UpdateStatus, then calculate the updated health.
terms: statusNumber - 1
Converts the user's 2 to list index 1.
ChangeStatus(section, selectedStatus)
Passes two inputs: 3 and Closed. These become parameters section and newStatus.
Contains / !
Contains asks whether the value is in the allowed list. ! means reject when it is not.
RiskStatus = newStatus
This assignment changes data. It is the line that actually closes the risk.
return true
Reports success to the waiting if in UpdateStatus. It does not print anything.
public ItemStatus RiskStatus { get; private set; } = ItemStatus.Closed;
Other code can read RiskStatus. Only Project's own code can assign it directly. New objects begin with Closed; ChangeStatus later applies validated changes.
more: ChangeStatus calls GetAllowedStatuses(3) again. Closed is in the returned list, so Contains returns true. The ! changes that to false, so return false is skipped. Section 3 selects RiskStatus; the assignment closes the risk. return true then resumes the waiting if in UpdateStatus. The property declaration shown here is a reference, not an extra instruction executed at this point.

title: Calculate and display the new health
plain: The risk is now Closed, so both open-risk conditions are false. Inventory's milestone is due in the future, so the overdue check is false. CalculateHealth returns OnTrack, and UpdateStatus prints it.
say: Health is calculated from the current data. Closing the risk removed Inventory's warning condition. The AI had no role in this calculation.
why: Checking the most serious condition first gives OffTrack priority. There is no stored Health property to become stale.

blocks.label: 2 · Apply the health rules and return

next: UpdateStatus ends and Main resumes at its menu case.
terms: AND: both conditions must be true.
RiskImpact >= 4
An open risk with impact at least 4 makes the project OffTrack.
HasValue / Value.Date
Check that a due date exists, then read its date. Missing dates are allowed.
< DateTime.Today
Earlier than today means overdue. Due today is not late.
return HealthStatus.OnTrack
Ends this method with the enum value OnTrack. Each earlier return would also end it immediately.
more: Otherwise any open risk or late unfinished milestone means AtRisk. A late task alone does not affect these rules. Priority score is likelihood × impact, but health does not use that product: an open risk with likelihood 1 and impact 4 still makes its project OffTrack.

title: Return to the menu, then exit
plain: UpdateStatus finishes. Main's break leaves the switch, and while displays the menu again. If you now enter 5, Main prints Goodbye and returns. That ends this application.
say: Methods return to their callers. The application ends when Main returns, not when we reach the end of some other method or source file.
why: The loop lets you do several operations during one run. Restarting creates fresh examples because there is no save file.

blocks.label: Back in Main: repeat or exit

values: Main returns; the HTTP client is disposed
next: To learn the AI path, reopen Inventory's risk or start a fresh session, then use the Local AI tab.
terms: break versus return
break leaves this switch. return in Main leaves Main and ends this program.
case null
If input ends, exit cleanly rather than looping forever.
Reopen before AI
From the menu enter 3 → 2 → 3 → 1 to reopen Inventory's risk. Then AI uses 4 → 2 → y.

title: Tell C# where the local AI lives
plain: First, look at the connection settings. This is setup context, not an execution step. Bionic runs the model on your computer. These two constants tell the tracker where to send requests and which model to select. They are not a model implementation or an API key.
say: I connected the app to Bionic's local API. This address points to my own computer, and this model key selects Qwen 3.5 9B.
why: Constants keep both connection settings in one place. They are not secret, and this local connection needs no OpenAI key.
values: Bionic's local server running; Qwen loaded
next: Main creates HttpClient, the object that sends the requests.
terms: const string
A text value fixed in the program code. Change it here and rebuild if the local port or model key changes.
A loopback address: the same computer. This request is not addressed to a cloud provider.
The port number identifying this local server's connection point.
API
An agreed way for programs to communicate. The C# app talks to an API, not by typing into Bionic's chat window.
Local model
A separately installed model loaded into memory by the Bionic runtime. The C# file does not contain or train Qwen.
more: Use Bionic's Settings → Local Model API to enable/check the server. Its local API uses the LM Studio runtime underneath; you can use Bionic as requested. Keep the runtime running while presenting. The app sends no model-download or model-load commands. It checks readiness before requesting a reply. If the model's state changes between those requests, the server may reload it.

title: Create the request-sending object
plain: Main creates one HttpClient and reuses it for AI requests. HTTP is a set of rules for requests and responses between programs. HttpClient is the .NET class that handles those exchanges.
say: I used HttpClient, which .NET already provides. I created one client in Main and passed it to the AI methods. I did not write my own networking system.
why: Reusing one client is simple. A timeout prevents this console action from waiting forever on a stalled HTTP request.

blocks.label: One client for this program run
Imports used by the request code — not an execution step

values: Our variable referring to its object
next: The user chooses menu 4; Main passes this same client into ReviewRiskAsync.
terms: new HttpClient()
Creates an object from the built-in HttpClient class.
using before the variable
Releases this disposable client when Main ends. It is different from a using import at the top of a file.
TimeSpan.FromSeconds(120)
Builds the duration value assigned to Timeout.
System.Text.Json
The namespace providing JsonSerializer and JsonDocument. JSON is structured text containing named values and lists.
Where HttpClient comes from
It is in System.Net.Http, included by this project's enabled ImplicitUsings. No extra NuGet package was added.
more: C# is the language. .NET provides types such as HttpClient, List, Task, and JsonDocument and runs the built app. Visual Studio is the editor/build/debug tool. Program and Project are the two application classes we authored; they are not the only library types used.

title: Menu 4 previews the data
plain: From a fresh session, enter 4, then project 2, then y. ReviewRiskAsync selects the existing Inventory object, checks that its risk is open, shows what will be sent, and asks for confirmation.
say: I preview the selected project's risk information and get confirmation before making the request. This keeps the AI step clear in the demonstration.
why: Only one risk exists per project, so no separate risk ID is needed. Selecting a closed risk or cancelling makes no AI request.

title: Understand the AI method's inputs
plain: ExplainRiskAsync receives the HTTP client and the selected project. It rejects a closed risk or out-of-range ratings before contacting Bionic. Then it asks which matching Qwen instance is loaded.
say: I pass existing objects as method inputs: the client for communication, and the project for the facts. The AI method eventually returns text.
why: Checking here also protects this method when called by tests or future code that bypasses the menu.

title: GET checks that Qwen is ready
plain: The client retrieves the model list from the local server. The code reads that JSON, finds our exact ModelKey, then looks for an ID in its loaded_instances list. It returns that ID to ExplainRiskAsync.
say: My first request checks readiness. A downloaded model is not necessarily loaded, so I look for a matching copy in memory before asking for an answer.
why: This prevents silently using a different model and gives a useful message when Qwen is unavailable.

blocks.label: Read the model list and find a loaded instance

values: Loaded Qwen ID; null if not found
next: Return to ExplainRiskAsync at line 164; if an ID was found, prepare the prompt.

Sends an HTTP GET and returns the response body as text when awaited.
CancellationTokenSource
Creates a stop signal scheduled after five seconds for this model-list request.
JsonDocument.Parse(json)
Reads the JSON text into a structure the code can inspect.
GetProperty / EnumerateArray / GetString
Read a named JSON value, visit each element of a JSON list, and extract text respectively.

Skip a model whose key does not match and move to the next one.

more: Illustrative shape, not a live reply: {"models":[{"key":"qwen/qwen3.5-9b","loaded_instances":[{"id":"qwen-example-instance"}]}]}. The key identifies the model; the loaded instance ID is what the next chat request uses. This GET does not ask Qwen to generate text.

title: Build the prompt from C# values
plain: A prompt is the text sent to the model. This line combines the project name, the already-calculated health, and the selected project's risk details.
say: I build a short prompt from our fictional data. C# calculates the health and risk score before the model sees the information. I ask the model to explain those facts.
why: Sending the selected risk's facts is enough for this demo. The request does not need the whole project repository.
next: Package this string with the model ID and answer instructions.
terms: string prompt
A local text variable, not a method, model, or class.
$"...{project.Name}..."
String interpolation inserts the property's value into the text.
\n
An escape sequence adding a line break.
+ project.GetRiskDetails()
Call the project's method and append the text it returns.
CalculateRiskScore()
Returns RiskLikelihood multiplied by RiskImpact. AI does not invent these ratings.
more: Example prompt begins: Fictional project: Inventory System / C# project health: OffTrack / Risk: Scanner hardware may arrive late. It also includes the risk owner, status, ratings, score, scenario, and current plan. It does not send unrelated task or milestone details.

title: Turn the request into JSON
plain: JsonSerializer.Serialize turns a temporary C# object's properties into JSON text. The API expects these named pieces: model, input, system_prompt, and request settings.
say: I package the model ID and prompt in the format Bionic expects. The serializer handles quotation marks and special characters so I do not build JSON by hand.
why: An anonymous object avoids creating a separate request class for this one operation. The project still has two authored application classes.
values: Our prompt containing the fictional facts
Instructions about answer format and limits
next: Wrap the JSON as an HTTP body, then send it.
terms: Creates an anonymous object. C# infers its properties' names and types; we do not write a named request class.
model,
Shorthand for a property named model containing the variable model's value.
input = prompt
input is the API's property name. prompt is our local string supplied as its value.
system_prompt
Instructions asking for Risk, Why, and Next action, with no invented extra events. Instructions do not guarantee accurate wording.
reasoning / stream / store
Requests reasoning off, one complete reply instead of streamed pieces, and no stored chat through this API.
max_output_tokens / integrations
Limits output to 500 model tokens (pieces of text, not necessarily words) and enables no integrations/tools. A model token is unrelated to a cancellation token.
more: The JSON envelope carries text; it does not give Qwen permission to edit C# objects. We do not execute the model's reply as code. It may make an inaccurate suggestion, but we only display the words.

title: POST is where the real AI call happens
plain: This is the actual request for generation. StringContent holds the JSON body. PostAsync sends it to the local chat URL. await waits for the response, and the next line checks for an HTTP failure.
say: This PostAsync call is where I ask local Qwen for an answer. The body contains the prompt and settings. I await the response, then check that the HTTP request succeeded.
why: HTTP lets the C# app and the local model server communicate through a documented interface, without automating a chat window.
values: JSON text: model, input, instructions, settings
An HTTP response object, not yet the final text
next: Read the response body and extract its final message.
terms: using StringContent body = new StringContent(...)
Create the request-body object. using releases it at the end of this scope.
Encoding.UTF8
Encodes text characters as bytes for transmission.
"application/json"
The content-type label telling the server that the body is JSON.
HttpResponseMessage
The .NET type representing the server's HTTP response.
response
Our local variable holding that response object.
client.PostAsync(URL, body)
Call a method on our HttpClient object. First argument: where to send. Second argument: what to send.
await
Wait for completion before the next statement runs. Async methods need no manually created thread here.
EnsureSuccessStatusCode()
Raises an exception for an unsuccessful HTTP status, so a catch returns a readable error.
more: The complete expression is: response = await client.PostAsync(BionicUrl + "/api/v1/chat", body). Read it as: 'Send this body to the local chat address; when the request completes, store its response.' The model generates the answer inside the separate runtime, not inside this C# line.

title: Unpack the reply and return words
plain: The response arrives as JSON. Parse reads its structure; the loop keeps entries marked message and collects their content. The method returns the assembled text to ReviewRiskAsync, which prints it.
say: I do not print raw JSON. I extract the final message content, return it as a string, and use Console.WriteLine to show it.
why: The API can include entries besides a final message. Filtering message entries keeps the display focused on the answer.

blocks.label: Extract final text and return it
The waiting caller resumes and prints it

values: Example advice. (illustration, not a live answer)
next: Review the error path, then rehearse the explanation.
terms: ReadAsStringAsync()
Reads the response body as text. Its await finishes before Parse inspects that text.
data.RootElement.GetProperty("output")
Reads the response's output list.
foreach (JsonElement output ...)
Visits each structured entry. This loop processes response entries, not project items.
output.GetProperty("type").GetString() == "message"
Checks which entries contain the final message.
StringBuilder / AppendLine
StringBuilder is a .NET class. new StringBuilder() creates a text-collecting object, and answer refers to it. AppendLine is a method that adds text and a line break to that object.
answer.ToString().Trim()
Converts collected content to one string and removes outer whitespace.
return versus WriteLine
return gives text back to the caller; WriteLine displays it. They are different actions.
more: The StringBuilder named answer inside ExplainRiskAsync and the string named answer inside ReviewRiskAsync are different local variables. The return value connects them. An empty or whitespace-only response becomes a helpful error message, never a fake AI answer.

title: If AI is unavailable, keep the tracker usable
plain: The expected networking, timeout, and response-format errors are caught and turned into readable messages. The same console method prints them and returns to the menu.
say: I handle common failures so the tracker still works without AI. A failed request produces an error message, not a stored answer pretending to be live.
why: A local model is a separate running service. It can be stopped, unloaded, slow, or return an unexpected response.
values: Unchanged by both success and failure
next: Use the Talk & demo tab to practice the complete explanation.
terms: catch (HttpRequestException)
Handles network problems and failed HTTP status checks.
catch (OperationCanceledException)
Handles cancellation/timeouts. The model-list timeout is five seconds; the chat request timeout is 120 seconds.
JsonException
JSON text could not be read.
KeyNotFoundException / InvalidOperationException
Expected response fields were missing or had incompatible types.
What this does not promise
These catches handle expected failures, not every possible bug or computer configuration. A prompt also cannot guarantee the model's factual accuracy.
more: For a timed presentation, demonstrate status changes first, reopen Inventory's risk, then request AI as your final console action. If it takes more than ten seconds, show the clearly labelled recorded example and finish speaking while the live request is pending. You cannot enter another menu choice until this operation returns.
